name: netdust-agent
description: Netdust two-layer agent harness — a SKELETON layer (steps, gates, ordering: the harnessed-development intake router (class dial A–F) → two spines meeting at an enforced seam: planning (brainstorm→spec→plan+gates→analyze, stops at an approved gate-checked tasks.md, planned inline while the human is steering or by a dispatched background planner when unattended) and building (refuses to start without that artifact; execute→test→review→shake-out→finish, owns the armed /loop). Building Stage 2 runs a tier-conditional test/dev split: for Tier-A security-boundary tasks (auth/guards, untrusted parsing, migrations) a plan-designated independent test-author writes the task's RED test from the contract before the implementer greens it — no agent grades its own homework where it matters most; other tasks run solo RED-first TDD; the mode is set in the plan's Test-author field and machine-checked by gate-check.py's test-author-mode check. Plus the gates the spines fire: testing-workflow, threat-modeling, architecture-invariants, feature-acceptance, test-effectiveness, shake-out, compounding, standards-gate; with writing-plans + finishing-a-branch deferred to their superpowers bases and the process retro to the /evaluate command) and a CRAFT layer (gerund-named how-to the harness reaches for at each step: writing-tests, designing-apis, building-frontend, engineering-context, versioning-with-git, driving-the-browser, refining-ideas, sourcing-from-docs, doubting-decisions, simplifying-code, deploying; plus the dev-stack infra skill). Naming convention: gerund = craft (how), phase/gate noun = harness (when/whether). The spec stage: superpowers:brainstorming authors specs/<feature>/spec.md to the spec-authoring skill's stated artifact contract (prioritized P1/P2/P3 stories whose boundaries become the review clusters, measurable SC-n success criteria shake-out signs off against, and an Assumptions section for every default chosen on the user's behalf) — there are no artifact templates, because a skeleton whose untouched state passes a gate is itself the defect, and the deterministic bin/gate-check.py HALTs on an unresolved [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] marker or a success criterion carrying no number. Open questions are handed back, never resolved by picking a plausible default. All tooling is self-contained in bin/ (gate-check.py, loop-check.py, run-*.py — bare python3, no third-party imports, no external CLI) and the scripts are the single definition of the artifact shape, so every gate binds on every project instead of degrading to self-attestation where a toolchain is missing; the spec-authoring / spec-analysis / constitution-bridge gates and SubagentStop's standards backstop run unconditionally — keystone: the handoff is tasks.md, and it is never executed flat. Adds run-observability: an in-loop event trace (run-trace.py, single-writer convergence point, `show --durations` for per-segment timings) + a deterministic evaluator rubric (run-score.py) graded from documented thresholds + a read-only cost report (run-cost.py: per-dispatch/per-stage token tables mined from local transcripts), surfaced in /shakeout and pointed to by /evaluate — report-only, zero new gates. Built on superpowers (base) + addyosmani/agent-skills (craft fills, MIT) with Netdust discipline as the authoritative spine. Standalone and self-contained — the full harness, specialist reviewer agents, hooks, and commands all live here, with no dependency on any other Netdust plugin.
